summary: Whakatāne Airport (WHK) is a regional airport serving the Eastern Bay of Plenty on New Zealand's North Island, located about 7 km north of Whakatāne town. It functions as the main gateway for visitors heading to White Island (Whakaari), one of the world's most accessible active marine volcanoes. The airport primarily handles Air New Zealand turboprop services linking the region with Auckland.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly from Whakatāne Airport?
A: Air New Zealand operates scheduled turboprop services from Whakatāne, with the main route being to Auckland.

Q: How far is the airport from Whakatāne town centre?
A: The airport is roughly 7 km north of the town centre, typically a 10-minute drive.

Q: Is the airport used for tours to White Island?
A: Yes, Whakatāne is the primary departure point for boat and helicopter tours to White Island (Whakaari), and the airport accommodates charter flights and scenic operators.

Q: Does the airport operate after hours?
A: The airport is generally open during scheduled service times only; passengers should confirm flight schedules as there is no 24-hour terminal service.
transport_tips: Taxis and rental cars are available at the terminal, though booking in advance is recommended due to limited availability. Parking is free and located directly outside the small terminal building. If heading to White Island boat tours, many operators offer pickup transfers with advance arrangement.
local_tip: Time your arrival to coincide with low tide at Ōhope Beach, voted one of New Zealand's best beaches and only a 15-minute drive from the airport — it's the perfect way to break up a travel day.
